newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bread rye supply adequate, but quality down.
newsitem.headline: German bread rye supply adequate, but quality down.

text.p: Germany's 1996 bread rye crop was sufficient for milling industry requirements in the 1996/97 season, although bread qualities had suffered from adverse weather, the state quality assessment centre for grain, potatoes and fats (BAGKF) in Detmold said.
Some 80 percent of the total 4.17 million tonne crop qualified for baking purposes, said BAGKF in a report which it made available to Reuters.
The crop was down by 7.8 percent from last year, when theoretically 100 percent qualified for baking.
But marketing patterns in recent years had shown only one-third of the crop normally goes into human consumption.
The area was down by 6.4 percent at 806,000 hectares and average yields down 1.5 percent at 5.17 tonnes per ha.
BAGKF said the extremely cold winter, followed by a cool summer and rain during harvesting, damaged crops especially badly in Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia.
Lower Saxony harvested 911,000 tonnes and Brandenburg 865,000 tonnes.
Yields were highest in North-Rhine Westphalia at 7.01 tonnes per ha, 35 percent up from the national average.
Thuringia, Schleswig-Holstein and Rhineland-Palatinate each achieved 6.0 tonnes and Brandenburg, at the bottom of the list, just 3.91 tonnes.
